text: Paul was an usher at Carnegie Hall, and on concert nights he always arrived early, wandering through the picture gallery before the doors opened to the public. <break time="0.8s" /> Once he had put on his uniform, which was one of the few that at all approached fitting, Paul became vivacious and animated, and he felt like a different person. <break time="0.8s" /> He was a model usher, running up and down the aisles with gracious smiles, as though it were a great reception and he were the host of the evening. <break time="0.8s" /> When the symphony began, Paul sank into one of the rear seats with a long sigh of relief, and the first notes seemed to free some hilarious spirit within him. <break time="0.8s" /> It struggled there like the Genius in the bottle found by the Arab fisherman, and as the lights danced before his eyes, the hall blazed into unimaginable splendor. <break time="0.8s" /> It was not that symphonies, as such, meant anything in particular to Paul, but the music carried him away from everything that was dull and ugly in his life. <break time="0.8s" /> After one concert, Paul followed the German soloist to her hotel and stood outside in the rain, watching the doors open and close upon a world of warmth and light. <break time="0.8s" /> He longed to enter that fairy world, but when the cold rain soaked his clothes, he wondered whether he was destined always to shiver in the black night outside.
